He was twice the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League Defensive Player of the Year]], in 2007 and 2008. He was an [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague First Team]] selection in [[2007–08 Euroleague|2008]]. == High school career == Terence Morris played his high school basketball for [[Governor Thomas Johnson High School]] in [[Frederick, Maryland]], leading the TJ Patriots to the Maryland Class 3A state title as a senior in 1997. He played under former TJ Patriots coach Tom Dickman, who until recently was the record holder for wins by a public school coach in Maryland with 592 wins in 29 seasons. ==College career== A {{convert|6|ft|9+1/2|in|m|sigfig=3|abbr=on}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?gamecode=213&pcode=LTS|title=MORRIS, TERENCE - Welcome to EUROLEAGUE BASKETBALL|date=March 23, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080323192646/https://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?gamecode=213&pcode=LTS |archive-date=2008-03-23 }} [[forward (basketball)|forward]] from the [[University of Maryland, College Park]], Morris was hailed as one of the best prospects in all of college basketball after his sophomore season in 1998–99. But while the consensus was that he would have been a Top-5 pick in the [[1999 NBA draft]] had he left school after that year along with teammate [[Steve Francis]], Morris instead opted to return to Maryland for his junior and senior seasons, and his draft stock dropped after two less individually successful campaigns. Morris helped play Maryland to the first Final Four in school history during the [[2001 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]] to cap his senior season. ==Professional career== ===NBA=== Morris was eventually selected by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] with the 33rd pick of the [[2001 NBA draft]],{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/draft2001/news/draft_order.html |title=NBA Draft 2001 |work=nba.com |access-date=2011-01-29}} and his draft rights were immediately traded to the [[Houston Rockets]], with whom he played two seasons ([[2001–02 NBA season|2001]]–[[2002–03 NBA season|2003]]). He then spent the 2003–04 season in the [[NBA G League|NBDL]] with the [[Columbus Riverdragons]] (now known as the [[Austin Spurs]]), and signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in September, 2004, but was waived before the season started. He signed with the [[Orlando Magic]] in September 2005. He earned a roster spot for the remainder of the season, but was again waived in February 2006. Morris' final NBA game was played on February 14, 2006, in a 93 - 107 loss to the Miami Heat where Morris only played for 37 seconds and recorded no stats. ===Europe=== After being waived by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in 2004, he decided to move to Europe and signed with [[Apollon Patras B.C.|Apollon Patras]] of the [[Greek Basket League|Greek League]]. Morris began the 2006–07 season unaffiliated to a team, but in December 2006, he signed with the [[Ligat Winner|Israeli League]] club [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.|Hapoel Jerusalem]] until the end of the season. With Hapoel he won an [[Israeli Basketball State Cup|Israeli State Cup]]. On June 13, 2007, he signed with the [[EuroLeague]] club [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/item/13621|title=Maccabi inks big man Morris|website=Welcome to EUROLEAGUE BASKETBALL|date=8 September 2023 }} He was twice the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League Defensive Player of the Year]], in 2007 and 2008. On May 3, 2008, Morris won a place in the [[2007–08 Euroleague|2007–08]] All-[[EuroLeague]] First team as a result of his play and the fact that his team reached the [[2008 Euroleague Final Four|EuroLeague Final]]. He then transferred to the [[Russian Basketball Super League 1|Russian Super League]] club [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]]{{Cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/item/33301|title=CSKA signs Terence Morris, Sasha Kaun|website=Welcome to EUROLEAGUE BASKETBALL|date=8 September 2023 }} and he reached another EuroLeague competition final in the [[2008–09 Euroleague|2008–09 season]]. In 2009, he joined the [[Liga ACB|Spanish ACB League]] club [[FC Barcelona Basquet|FC Barcelona]],{{Cite web|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/20090711/terrence-morris-atado_53741966043.html|title=Terrence Morris, atado|date=July 11, 2009|website=Mundo Deportivo}} with whom he won his first EuroLeague competition in 2010.[http://www.europapress.cat/esports/noticia-barcelona-aconsegueix-seva-segona-eurolliga-exhibicio-culmina-brillant-temporada-20100510075135.html El Barça, campió d'Europa 2010]
